scope: Theorem 1.1 (Routing density and representation contraction) of the manuscript “Routing densities and representation contraction for Thorp sweeps” (preprints/Routing-densities-and-representation-contraction-for-Thorp-sweeps-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4e5fbcff0dec65fd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are absolute constants η, c, C > 0 such that, with a = 1/1000, log Ey∼uN,k Rx(y)1+a ≤ Ck(k/N)η (1 ≤ k ≤ N), uniformly over every starting injection x. For every sufficiently large dyadic N and every nontrivial irreducible representation, TN (λ) = 0 or ∥TN (λ)∥op ≤ D−c λ . Consequently an absolute number of forward sweeps has worst-start total-variation distance from uniform tending to zero as d → ∞.
